title: 5 K-Dramas to Watch If You Loved Teach You a Lesson
excerpt: Finished Netflix's #1 K-drama and need another? Five shows with the same righteous-anger energy — and where to stream each one.
author: StarScoop Daily Staff
imageAlt: Teach You a Lesson backdrop — similar K-dramas to watch next
metaDescription: K-dramas like Teach You a Lesson — five shows with the same revenge-thriller energy, what each does differently, and where to stream them.
content:
You finished all ten episodes and now nothing else looks appealing. Here are five K-dramas that scratch the same itch — and what each one does differently.

If you likedWatch
The vigilante justiceBloodhounds
The institutional angerSquid Game
The emotional weight underneathWhen Life Gives You Tangerines

1. Bloodhounds

Netflix · TMDB 4.2/5 · Complete

Two young boxers get pulled into the world of predatory private lending, and decide to do something about it.

Why it fits: this is the closest match on the list. Same structure — decent people using physical force against a system that exploits the vulnerable, because the legal route is useless. The fight choreography is genuinely excellent, and it's grounded rather than stylized.

What's different: the target is loan sharks rather than schools, so the villainy is financial. It's also less interested in institutional reform and more in personal loyalty.

2. Squid Game

Netflix · Complete

You have almost certainly heard of it, and if you came to K-dramas through Teach You a Lesson you may not have watched it.

Why it fits: the same fury at a system that grinds people down, taken to its furthest possible extreme. Both shows are fundamentally about debt — financial in one, moral in the other.

What's different: nobody wins. Teach You a Lesson gives you a partial victory; this offers none. Go in knowing it's considerably bleaker.

3. When Life Gives You Tangerines

Netflix · TMDB 4.4/5 · Complete

Widely cited as the most acclaimed Korean original on the platform.

Why it fits: this is the palate cleanser, and it's on the list deliberately. The thing that actually made Teach You a Lesson land wasn't the violence — it was Ga-yun, and grief, and a man who couldn't let go. This is that emotional register with none of the punching.

What's different: completely. No crime, no vigilantes. If you want more action, skip it. If you noticed the show was sadder than it looked, start here.

4. Mirzapur — For the Same Energy, Different Country

Prime Video · Complete seasons available

Not Korean, but worth the detour if what you liked was small-town power structures and institutional rot.

Why it fits: the Indian equivalent of the register — crime, family, and a place where the law is one option among several. Our full Mirzapur breakdown covers whether it's for you.

What's different: considerably more violent, and far less interested in redemption.

5. Scam 1992 — If You Liked the Systems Detail

SonyLIV · 10 episodes · Complete

Why it fits: one of the underrated pleasures of Teach You a Lesson is that it explains how the institutional machinery actually works — the bureau's remit, the political pressure, the paperwork. Scam 1992 does that with financial crime and does it better than almost anything.

What's different: no action whatsoever. It's the highest-rated Indian series ever made and it's about bank receipts. Our breakdown explains why that works.

Where to Start

Pick by what you actually want:

  • More of the same → Bloodhounds. Closest match, same satisfaction.
  • Something heavier → Squid Game. Same anger, no relief.
  • The emotional version → When Life Gives You Tangerines.
  • Systems and detail → Scam 1992.

One honest note: streaming availability shifts by region, and Korean titles in particular move between services outside the US. Check your local Netflix listing before planning an evening.

Haven't finished it yet? Our Teach You a Lesson ending explained covers who killed Ga-yun and what the final scene means. For more streaming picks, see our weekend guide.
